headline: RBA likely done on rate cuts, with impact more visible in AUD cross rates than AUD/USD
reasoning: Peter Dragicevich believes the RBA is most likely finished with its easing cycle. He expects this domestic story around slower growth and a done RBA to manifest more clearly in cross rates (e.g. AUD/NZD) rather than in AUD/USD, which he expects will remain under some pressure over the next 6 to 12 months.
quote: Most likely my view that they're done that will probably come through more clearly on the cross rates rather than against the US dollar, which is probably going to remain under pressure a little bit over the next kind of 6 to 12 months.
episode_title: The data set to shape the next currency moves

headline: Japanese yen is undervalued and likely to be one of the biggest FX movers over the next 12 months, with asymmetric upside
reasoning: Dragicevich sees the yen as fundamentally undervalued, noting that the weak yen is adding to Japanese inflation, which will require the Bank of Japan to be more aggressive with rate hikes. Combined with the Fed holding steady on rate expectations, this should drive yen strength. He also points to positive signs in Japan's growth outlook. He views the risk as highly asymmetric — limited downside, significant upside — and notes that when the yen turns, it historically moves very aggressively.
quote: I think fundamentally the yen is too weak. If you think about the policy outlook, you know, the weaker yen is adding to inflation in Japan. It will mean the Bank of Japan has to be a bit more aggressive in terms of rate hikes going forward. If you get that plus obviously the fed not doing anything in terms of rate expectations, you should see the yen strengthened. But even fundamentally, you know, there are positive signs coming through in Japan's economy in terms of growth. Picking up obviously that inflation story, as I said. So you know, I think it's undervalued. And we should see again, medium term the yen strengthen probably will be one of the biggest movers over the next 12 months. I think it's just asymmetric risks. There's a there's a small chance it could become a little bit weaker, but there's a much bigger chance that it could strengthen a lot. And and historically when it turns, it turns very aggressively.
episode_title: The data set to shape the next currency moves

headline: US dollar weakness driven by softer data and Fed rate hike expectations falling, not a structural debasement story
reasoning: Peter argues the recent USD weakness reflects softer US economic data, declining inflation surprises, and reduced probability of a Fed rate hike in September (now around 40%), rather than any structural debasement. The Treasury buyback announcement is seen as a signal rather than a meaningful policy shift. At the long end, bond supply from large US budget deficits, debt rollovers, and AI firm capital raises is outstripping demand, keeping long-term rates higher for longer. He does not expect the Jackson Hole speech from new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh to provide near-term guidance.
quote: Look the basement trade always flares up whenever the US dollar loses some ground and then it goes away whenever the dollar strengthens. So I don't really think it's a debasement story. If you run through the list of factors of why the US dollar has been weakening the last probably six weeks or so, you know, the US data has been a bit softer. Data surprises have started to come down. Inflation pulse is a bit softer as well. So the markets kind of reduced the probabilities of a fed rate hike say in September. It's now sitting at about 40%.
episode_title: The data set to shape the next currency moves

headline: AUD/NZD cross rate expected to fall as RBNZ lifts rates and NZD strengthens
reasoning: Dragicevich argues the RBNZ hit the economy hard during its tightening phase and then had to aggressively cut rates, but now needs to gradually remove accommodation by lifting rates higher. He expects the New Zealand economy to hold up, with a healing labour market providing momentum, which should help the NZD strengthen over the medium term and push AUD/NZD lower.
quote: The BNZ hit the economy very hard during the tightening phase to crush inflation. They did a great job, but it also hit the economy very hard and so they had to backpedal quite aggressively last year. And now they've got rates in a very accommodative territory. So what they need to do now going forward is to continue to just take away those rate cuts and lift interest rates a bit higher. It's not like they're hitting the brakes. It's akin to them taking their foot off the accelerator. So they're going to continue, I think to deliver more rate hikes. The New Zealand economy actually should hold up. There's a bit of momentum beneath the surface there. The labour market is healing and so it should help the kiwi kind of strengthen over the medium term. And as I said see Aussie Kiwi like crosses like that kind of fall back.
episode_title: The data set to shape the next currency moves

headline: Australian dollar looks stretched around 72 US cents; model fair value closer to 70 cents with RBA likely done hiking
reasoning: Peter's models suggest the AUD is overvalued at 72 US cents and should be closer to 70 cents. The domestic Australian economy is slowing, unemployment is rising, and he believes the RBA will not hike again despite talking tough. Interest rate differentials are moving against the AUD. He expects the AUD to trade in a 70–72 range against the USD over the next 6–12 months but to underperform on cross rates, losing ground against the euro and NZD as the domestic slowdown becomes more apparent.
quote: I think the dollar's probably a bit stretched. Um, the way I kind of frame it is up around 72. It's looking too high. My models are kind of saying at the moment it should be closer to 70 rather than 72. If you think about the dollar story, yes, it has given the ozone a boost. But when you think about things domestically, the economy is slowing. The cracks in the labour market are starting to widen given unemployment's up, you know. Will the RBA really hike again? I don't think so. I think they're going to talk tough for a little while longer. But the data is turning, starting to turn against them so that the need to actually deliver more tightening is probably fading.
episode_title: The data set to shape the next currency moves

headline: PCE inflation data on Wednesday seen as near-term catalyst for further USD weakness ahead of Jackson Hole
reasoning: Peter expects the upcoming PCE inflation print to soften, which would further reduce the probability of a September Fed rate hike and weigh on the USD. He notes PCE has been the only inflation measure holding up due to a basket weighting issue, and expects a bigger drop next month when the basket is reweighted. Offsetting factors include geopolitical tensions and elevated oil prices, which support the dollar given the US is now a net energy exporter.
quote: I think probably the near-term catalyst for the dollar might just be that PC inflation data out on Wednesday night. Um, the PCs, the only kind of measure of inflation that's actually been holding up. And that's because of a weighting issue in terms of the basket. So it probably will fall back. And then next month the PC probably is going to get rerated. So we'll get a bigger drop there. So that will probably ah just lessen the chances of that fed rate hike coming in September. Um, and then the dollar could could weaken a little bit.
episode_title: The data set to shape the next currency moves
